merger_description:
General Dental Holdings Pty Ltd (trading as **Impression Dental Group**) proposes to acquire 100% of the assets of the dental practice known as Blackburn Clinic Dental Centre (**Blackburn Dental Centre**) through a business sale agreement.

Blackburn Dental Centre is owned by dentists Dr Andrea Manley and Dr Konstantina Liosis, both personally and through a combination of corporate entities and corporate trusts and supplies general dental services from its clinic in Blackburn, in the eastern suburbs of Melbourne, Victoria.

Impression Dental Group is an Australian-based dental support organisation that provides centralised services including recruitment, payroll, marketing, IT, finance, and operations, to enable dental practitioners to focus on providing dental services. It currently owns and supports 35 independently branded dental practices in Australia which provide dental services to the public, but Impression Dental Group currently does not have any practices in Melbourne’s eastern suburbs.

Impression Dental Group is controlled by Genesis Capital (**Genesis**), an Australian-based private equity firm that invests in businesses operating in the healthcare sector.

Genesis Capital’s investments also include Pacific Smiles Group which sets up new dental centres from which dentists run their practice and provides operational support. Pacific Smiles Group has over 120 dental centres across Australia, including 3 in neighbouring suburbs to Blackburn (Doncaster East, Ringwood and Glen Waverley). Pacific Smiles Group’s dental centres are typically located inside shopping centres and operate under the Pacific Smiles Dental and nib Dental Care brands on the East Coast.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. the parties’ combined share in the supply of general dental
services to customers in the local area surrounding
Blackburn Dental Centre is low and the increase in share of
supply arising from the Acquisition would be small
b. there are numerous alternative suppliers of general dental
services to customers in the local area surrounding
Blackburn Dental Centre.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
